iterationGoal: Take the previous generated image and add subtle but clearly readable parkour training modules to the scene, so the viewer instantly understands this is a 'parkour summer stage at the beach' — not just a kid leaping at the beach. Keep everything else exactly as it was: same character, outfit, pose direction, style, color palette, lighting, sky, sun, umbrella, beach chair, basket with baguette, striped towel, sand dune, lagoon, pier, seagulls.

newElement_1.name: Wooden parkour vault box
newElement_1.description: A solid cube-shaped plywood vault box (parkour module), roughly 70cm tall, made of warm light pine wood with a slightly darker wood top, a single thin coral red (#FF6B6B) accent stripe along the top edge
newElement_1.placement: Centered on the wooden boardwalk in the foreground, directly underneath the leaping child — the child is clearly jumping OVER this box in a parkour vault move
newElement_1.perspective: Slight three-quarter view, sitting flat on the boardwalk planks, casting one soft navy cell-shaded shadow on the wood

newElement_2.name: Stack of soft foam training blocks
newElement_2.description: Two stacked rectangular gym foam blocks (parkour training props), top block electric blue (#006AFF), bottom block warm yellow (#FFD23F), clean flat cartoon shapes with bold navy outlines
newElement_2.placement: On the sandy dune area to the left of the umbrella, half-resting on the sand as if casually set up for training
newElement_2.size: Small secondary element, clearly smaller than the umbrella

newElement_3.name: Low parkour rail
newElement_3.description: A short horizontal metal bar (~60cm long, ~50cm tall) on two simple white posts, like a mini gymnastics balance bar, painted PKBA electric blue (#006AFF)
newElement_3.placement: Far right of the boardwalk near the water edge, partly behind the leaping child, secondary visual element
newElement_3.size: Small enough not to distract from the main vault action

characterAdjustment.pose: Refine the leap so the child is unambiguously vaulting OVER the new wooden parkour box: legs tucked or split with one leg leading the other, body angled forward across the box, arms outstretched for balance, hands free (not touching the box)
characterAdjustment.motionLines: Keep 3-5 short curved white motion lines, but place them so they wrap around the parkour box, reinforcing the vault motion direction
